[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
John Glasgow died intestate before 26 March 1789. On that date Peter Glasgow of West Nottingham certified that John was his uncle and had lived at his house about twenty-seven years. His estate inventory included eleven old shoemaker lasts. John Taylor received administration on 31 March. Peter described Taylor as his sister’s son, which does not itself make Taylor the deceased’s son.<ref>Chester County Register of Wills, original file 4015, West Nottingham, 1789, volume 03901–4050, portal pp. 1060–1066; Peter’s certificate p. 1065. [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=772934&page=1065&repo=r-24f48cc6 Official original]. Images inspected 23 October 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
Profile identity remains unresolved. No father, mother or exact birth/death date is supplied by the inspected estate. The 1792 John estate records a debt from a deceased John Glasgow shoemaker; the 1789 man is a probable identification of that debtor, not a proved relative of the 1792 John.
